item.title: 'It didn’t sit very well' - Julian Alvarez's Atletico Madrid teammates 'annoyed' by public transfer plea to join Barcelona
item.description: Julian Alvarez - Getty Images Julian Alvarez’s public transfer demand caused significant frustration within the Atletico Madrid dressing room, according to team-mate Alex Baena. The Argentina forward pushed for a summer move to Barcelona, leading to internal tension and a hostile reception from supporters at the Metropolitano. Alvarez transfer demands angered Atletico team-mates Alvarez's public plea to leave Atletico caused significant unrest among his team-mates. The Argentina international expressed a strong desire to secure a transfer away from the club in June, publicly stating that a move would be best for all parties. Barcelona emerged as the primary suitors for the highly-rated forward. Joan Laporta confirmed the Catalan club's interest in August, but Atletico firmly refused to sanction a sale during a drawn-out summer saga. The failed transfer resulted in a difficult situation for Alvarez in the Spanish capital. He faced intense scrutiny from supporters and sparked frustration from his colleagues inside the dressing room. Baena reveals dressing room frustrations Spain midfielder Baena has now shed light on exactly how the squad reacted to the transfer saga. Speaking to Cadena SER on Monday night, he admitted that Alvarez's public approach caused unnecessary friction behind the scenes. "It feels a bit strange when a team-mate says publicly that he wants to leave," Baena explained during the radio interview. "It didn’t sit very well with us. I can understand a player having doubts if a club like Barca or Real Madrid comes in for you, but, ultimately, it was the way he went about it that really annoyed us at Atletico." Rebuilding relationships at the Metropolitano Alvarez eventually apologised to Atletico fans in October following his controversial summer comments. While the intense whistling from the Metropolitano crowd at the start of the season has slightly subsided, some hostility remains clearly audible during matches. Despite the initial anger, Baena insists the squad is completely ready to move forward together. "We would have supported him regardless of what he decided to do," the midfielder added. "The important thing is that he is with us now, and we need to show him all the affection in the world." Simeone backs his star forward Diego Simeone is also eager to put the disruption behind them and focus entirely on the current campaign. Speaking at a press conference on Sunday, the manager stated that the club is patiently waiting for the striker to return to his best form. "He's a great player and we love him," Simeone told reporters. The Argentine coach will rely heavily on his forward.

item.title: Don’t Bench LaNorris Sellers If He Is Healthy For Arkansas
item.description: South Carolina Gamecocks quarterback LaNorris Sellers (16) throws a pass during a college football game between the University of Oklahoma Sooners (OU) and the South Carolina Gamecocks at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium in Norman, Okla., Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026. South Carolina won 42-25. The temptation to bench LaNorris Sellers for Saturday night against Arkansas is strong, but the move would be a mistake if he can go. South Carolina coach Shane Beamer told reporters on Sunday that the team expects their star quarterback to play despite the ankle injury. Beamer stated, “We fully expect him to play,” after Sellers completed medical tests that day, according to a report . The Gamecocks need their Heisman Trophy candidate on the field to keep their playoff hopes alive. Sellers showed his toughness by limping to a 41-yard touchdown in the win over Texas A&M on Saturday. He hurt his ankle in the second quarter but returned to finish the game. While he did not look like his usual self during the second half, the coaching staff designed plays to protect him. Beamer noted, “We feel good about his availability this weekend,” regarding the upcoming matchup. The only real concern is his pain tolerance and the swelling in that ankle, not a structural failure. The Trap Game Warning Pretty much the entire season has been dreadful for Arkansas, with just one SEC win. This makes the game a trap for the Gamecocks, especially with a night game in the SEC always scary for fans who have followed the program for decades. A loss to the Razorbacks would end all talk about a College Football Playoff spot and a second Heisman Trophy winner for the school. The upcoming showdown against Georgia in two weeks will hold no significance on the national stage if the team loses this weekend. Resting Sellers only makes sense if the injury is a high ankle sprain that could take weeks to heal. Beamer did not confirm it is that type of injury, though he acknowledged the swelling needs to go down. If the medical staff clears him, sitting him on the sideline is a risk the team cannot afford. The team should only consider resting him if they build a sizeable lead in the second half to avoid further injury. Heisman Stakes and Final Games Winning the last three games puts the Gamecocks in the College Football Playoff and secures a trip to New York for Sellers. Fans on social media think resting him is in the best interest of the team, but that logic fails if the opponent is weak. The priority is winning now, not protecting the quarterback for a future game that might not happen. Although Sellers skipped practice on Sunday evening and the Gamecocks do not train on Mondays, the coach remains confident. Beamer said, “Right now, it’s nothing that concerns us aside from his pain tolerance and getting some of the swelling down in that ankle.” The team will know more after the final medical review before the game.

item.title: Will Vikings Trade for QB After Disastrous Night for Wentz?
item.description: Nov 9, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz (11) reacts after a play during the third quarter against the Buffalo Bills at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images The Minnesota Vikings face a harsh reality after a disastrous Monday Night Football loss. Coach Kevin O’Connell refused to commit to a quarterback trade despite a historic collapse by Carson Wentz. The team sits at a crossroads following a 6-0 start that has turned into consecutive losses. O’Connell deferred to general manager Nolan Teasley after the 23-6 defeat to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night. A Historic Low for Wentz Carson Wentz delivered the worst performance by any starting quarterback in the NFL this season, before being replaced by Max Brosmer in the fourth quarter. Only 8 of 25 passes were completed for 81 yards, alongside two interceptions thrown. His 2.3 QBR marks the lowest score for any player in the league this year. This number is also the lowest for a Vikings quarterback since Tarvaris Jackson in 2006. ESPN reported that this was the third game this season where the team failed to score a touchdown. Troy Aikman voiced his frustration on the ESPN broadcast after the game. Aikman noted that Wentz nearly threw an interception at the end of the third quarter. “I haven’t had many starts over the last couple of years in general,” Wentz said, “but this one felt pretty terrible. I’m not going to lie. Yeah, this one wasn’t my favorite, that’s for sure.” Coach Owes the Fix O’Connell admitted he failed to get Wentz into a rhythm during the game. He tried various tools to help the quarterback but acknowledged the mistake. “We never got Carson in a rhythm,” Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said in his postgame press conference. The coach noted that he should have run the ball more rather than forcing passes on third down. An off-target rate of 38 percent ended the game for Wentz, representing the lowest figure in an NFL match this season. O’Connell said he wanted a balanced offense, but the plan fell apart. The Vikings are now stuck with a roster that cannot score points . O’Connell stated he would focus on the next game rather than immediate roster changes. “We’ve had dialogue about a lot of different positions,” O’Connell said. “Tight turnaround, obviously, playing the Monday night game, and we’ll get right to work on any potential moves that can be there. But really just focused on the game tonight, which was not good enough in any way, shape, or form.” The team must find a way to address the offense without waiting until the trade deadline passes.

item.title: Hornets’ Scoring Gap Widens As Cavaliers Prepare For Tuesday Clash
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets are averaging just 96.3 points per game, a number that looks low compared to the 117.0 points the Cleveland Cavaliers score every night. The home team trails the Cavaliers by a significant offensive margin as they prepare for Tuesday’s game, with the Cavaliers on a winning streak and the Hornets still searching for consistency. According to ESPN , the Hornets have lost their last six games in a row. That slide puts them in a bad spot right before they host a team that scores nearly 21 more points per game than they do. Two Teams in Different Spots Donovan Mitchell leads the Cavaliers with 24.0 points per game. He also shoots 48.8% from the field and 77.0% from the free-throw line, according to ESPN. His numbers show why Cleveland is so hard to stop. On the other side, Brandon Miller is the top scorer for the Hornets with 20.6 points per game. But Miller is shooting just 35.6% from the field. The difference in shooting efficiency is clear. Cleveland makes 46% of their shots while the Hornets only make 39% per ESPN. That seven-point gap in field goal percentage is a big reason why the Hornets have lost so many games lately. The Hornets also struggle to move the ball. They average 20.8 assists per game. The Cavaliers move the ball much better with 27.0 assists per game. More passes lead to better shots, and that helps explain the scoring difference. The Hornets need to find a way to get more players involved if they want to stop the bleeding. Without better ball movement, they will keep facing the same issues on Tuesday night. item.title: Watch: Gabriel Jesus left amazed by Barcelona teammate’s performance vs Atletico Madrid
item.description: Watch: Gabriel Jesus left amazed by Barcelona teammate’s performance vs Atletico Madrid Barcelona’s midfield maestro Pedri may have had a topsy turvy campaign so far, with his lowest point coming in the defeat against Real Madrid. The Spaniard was criticised for his lack of impact in El Clasico . This is coupled with the fact that Pedri is also not a regular for the Spanish national team. However, in Barcelona’s win over Atletico Madrid, Pedri once again showed what he is capable of, producing a solid performance even in the absence of the injured Rodri. Gabriel Jesus hails Pedri’s performance Pedri’s performance against Atletico Madrid did not go unnoticed either, with his own teammate Gabriel Jesus in awe of his display at the Metropolitano. As captured by the Movistar cameras, the Barça new signing was seen speaking to Alejandro Balde on the bench, where he praised Pedri’s performance. “What a player Pedri. An incredible player ,” said the Brazilian, who was left as an unused substitute in the narrow win over Atleti. Balde, too, responded to Gabriel Jesus’ comment, agreeing with the Brazilian’s assessment. “It is very good bro,” he replied. The comments from the two Barcelona stars is hardly surprising as Pedri was indeed a key operator in the middle of the park, especially in the second half where he was able to instill more control to the game and help Barcelona complete the comeback. Road ahead for Pedri Pedri played a crucial role in Barcelona’s win over Atletico Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The performance against Pedri should serve as a major confidence booster for Pedri, as he heads to the international break. The Barcelona star is a part of the Spanish contingent, which is expected to take on Czechia and England in the UEFA Nations League. Pedri is expected to feature prominently in both the matches, given that Rodri is no longer available to Luis de la Fuente due to an injury. Barcelona will hope Pedri can avoid any injuries, considering the fact that Rodri is already unavailable while Frenkie de Jong has just returned from a long injury layoff. Hansi Flick has already taken great care in maintaining game-time for Pedri. It will be disappointing if the Spaniard picks up an unfortunate knock during this international break.

item.title: Dan Orlovsky says what he’s seen Jordan Love do is ‘breaking the rules of football’
item.description: Photo by M. Anthony Nesmith/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After a shaky start to the season, the Green Bay Packers are establishing themselves as one of the real forces in the NFC. Jordan Love continues to impress at quarterback, and Sunday’s game against the New England Patriots was one of his best yet. On a day when Drake Maye threw three interceptions, Love ended the game having thrown for three touchdowns and 372 yards. It is hard not to be blown away by the level of football Love is currently playing at, and Dan Orlovsky has now even suggested that the standard being set by Love is so good that it is actually ‘breaking the laws of football’. Dan Orlovsky thinks no quarterback is playing better than Jordan Love Through his opening nine games of the season, Love has thrown 19 touchdowns and six interceptions. No other quarterback has thrown for more yards (2,618) than Love this season, with Orlovsky left staggered by how well the Packers’ QB is currently playing. “Realistically, guys, there is no reason Jordan Love should be playing this well. He should not be playing this well, and he just continues to play at a level that is very rare. Stephen A., they have drops, they have penalties, this is a makeshift offensive line, and they cannot run the football. Quarterbacks in that setting should not play as well as he is playing. He is breaking the rules of football, that is what he is doing. “It is not just that Jordan Love is playing at an MVP level. Jordan Love is breaking the rules of football right now, and that speaks to the context of how well he is playing.” However, Stephen A. Smith hit back at Orlovsky, claiming that he needs to see Love play at this level when it matters in the postseason. It has been six years since the Packers made it to the Conference Championship game, with consecutive years of being knocked out at the Wild Card Round over the last two years. “He can play. I’ve always said that. What I have said was I want to see him look the same come playoff time. And I got news for you, D.O., that opinion has not changed,” Smith replied. item.title: ‘Great dude’ – Logan Ryan reveals which quarterback has impressed him most this season
item.description: Photo by Ryan Kang/Getty Images Logan Ryan recently made an appearance on the Up & Adams show and was quizzed on which quarterback has impressed him most in the NFL this term. Josh Allen continues to earn plaudits for the Buffalo Bills after another stellar showing in their most recent game against the Minnesota Vikings. When Adams asked Ryan which quarterback has impressed him the most this season, he responded: “You know what, I got to go with, I got to go with, man, my guy Purdy. Put some respect on Purdy’s name. “Fred says all the time, this guy was, what is it, Mr Irrelevant last draft pick. “He’s getting it done all ways man against all odds, I love Purdy for that. Purdy and I did like breath work before every single practice. We did this thing where we practice our breathing. He has a nice little meditation thing he does and it gets him in the zone. He puts a lot of work in behind the scenes. “He’s a great dude, a great teammate. Put some respect on Purdy in the MVP race.” Purdy has 1,980 passing yards this season with a completion rate of 69.1 per cent as well as 17 touchdowns. His impressive form has helped the San Francisco 49ers go 7-1 so far, with their next outing taking place this Sunday against the 4-5 Dallas Cowboys. item.title: Real Madrid forward receives much-needed support from national teammates amid struggles
item.description: Real Madrid forward receives much-needed support from national teammates amid struggles Vinicius Jr. is going through a difficult spell at Real Madrid, but the forward continues to enjoy strong backing within the Brazil national team, where Carlo Ancelotti is confident he can help him recover his best form. According to AS , there is a strong belief among his international teammates that the Italian coach understands how to get the best out of the winger and can help him overcome his current struggles. The aforementioned claim is quite understandable because Ancelotti and Vinicius together enjoyed one of the most successful runs in Real Madrid’s history. Notably, the contrast between Vinicius’ club and international situations is becoming quite significant because at Madrid, his place in Jose Mourinho’s starting line-up has come under pressure following Yan Diomande’s emergence . In the national team setup, however, he remains an important figure under Ancelotti. Diomande’s emergence increases pressure on Vinicius at Real Madrid Vinicius Jr. is struggling for form this season. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) Vinicius’ difficult start to the season has given Mourinho a genuine selection dilemma . The Brazilian has managed just one goal and three assists in 12 appearances for Real Madrid, a return below the standards expected from a player who has previously been one of the club’s most influential attacking threats. Diomande, on his part, has made the competition more difficult. The Ivorian has impressed with his performances and offered Mourinho a productive alternative on the left wing. His emergence has also allowed the coach to make changes without weakening the team’s attacking threat. Brazil national team camp feels Ancelotti will help restore Vinicius’ form. (Photo by Wagner Meier/Getty Images) Vinicius is therefore no longer guaranteed a starting position, and Mourinho has also made clear that selection will depend on performances, although his public comments and treatment of the Brazilian indicate that he still wants to help him recover his best level . Ancelotti could provide the confidence Vinicius needs The international break offers Vinicius an opportunity to work with a coach who understands his game particularly well. Ancelotti helped develop the Brazilian into a decisive attacker during their time together at Real Madrid, and their relationship is an important source of confidence for the forward. The optimism within the Brazil camp is significant because Vinicius needs to rediscover the qualities that made him so difficult to defend against and for that, he needs support from teammates, be it from Brazil or from Real Madrid.

item.title: ‘So washed’ – NFL fans call out Troy Aikman over ‘ridiculous’ MNF comment
item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings fans were left with very little to applaud on Monday night against the Buffalo Bills, but Byron Murphy’s interception on Josh Allen certainly impressed Troy Aikman. Allen was able to throw for 234 yards on Monday night in Minnesota, but the Vikings’ incredible defense was able to limit him to just one touchdown thrown. The Bills’ quarterback attempted a 36-yard touchdown pass in the first quarter, which was intercepted by Murphy. As the Vikings’ cornerback returned it to around the halfway line, Aikman was left waxing lyrical about the interception: “One of the best plays I’ve ever seen.” Although no one will deny Murphy’s interception and return was impressive, there was a clear feeling among fans online that perhaps Aikman was taking his comments a little too far. NFL fans hit back at Troy Aikman’s praise of Byron Murphy’s interception DJ Moore was the intended receiver for Allen’s pass, but Murphy was able to fly in there and come away with the ball. A seriously impressive play, but one of the best ever seen? That felt like a slight exaggeration from Aikman . ‘Aikman is over it,’ replied one fan on X after seeing the clip of Aikman’s commentary. ‘Aikman is just there so he doesn’t get fined,’ another fan jokingly said in relation to Marshawn Lynch’s iconic interview. The colour commentator’s future with ESPN remains hanging in the balance as no new deal has been agreed between the two parties. Aikman’s commentary on Monday night clearly left a lot of people feeling as if he is now simply seeing out his time with the network. ‘That’s ridiculous, he would say that…’ replied another fan. ‘Troy is checked out,’ added another. Tony Romo featured on ESPN’s alternative coverage of Monday Night Football on the Field Pass show, which has left a number of viewers feeling as if the former CBS commentator was being ‘soft launched’ as Aikman’s future successor. ‘Troy so hyperbolic lol,’ one fan responded. ‘Hang them up Troy you are so washed,’ another even said. item.title: Wainwright gives Wales injury scare for All Blacks
item.description: Aaron Wainwright joined Leicester from Dragons for the start of the 2025-26 season [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Number eight Aaron Wainwright has emerged as a major injury concern for the Nations Championship game against New Zealand in Cardiff on Saturday. The 29-year-old picked up a leg injury and has since been seen in a protective boot. He did not train on Tuesday. Head coach Steve Tandy will name his team on Thursday and absence of the former Dragons player would be a major blow. Wainwright started in the 28-21 victory against Japan last Saturday and was the most experienced forward in the squad. The Leicester number eight, who was winning his 71st cap, is also Wales' most effective forward ball-carrier. New Zealand wing Will Jordan will miss the game because of a hamstring injury but centre Jordie Barrett is available for selection to face Wales after passing his head injury assessment (HIA) protocols. Smiling Rees-Zammit has no fear of All Blacks Wales should make fly-half change - Shanklin Basham in pole position Recalled Taine Basham would be the leading contender to replace Wainwright on Saturday, with Scarlets back-rower Taine Plumtree providing the other option in the squad. Basham was rewarded with a squad call-up having been the form number eight in Welsh domestic rugby this season. The Cardiff number eight has not played for Wales since the 2024 Six Nations, while his previous start to that was in 2022. After the All Blacks match, Wales will host Australia on 21 November, before the Nations Championship finals weekend at the end of the month, hosted by the Allianz Stadium at Twickenham. Wales currently lie fifth out of sixth in the northern hemisphere table after two wins from four matches. item.title: Bayern remain in talks to sign Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha
item.description: Bayern remain in talks to sign Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha was one of the options Bayern Munich explored last summer as the German champions searched for a new winger. According to multiple reports, Bayern were ready to splurge around €70 million on the 18-year-old, but the move ultimately didn't materialise due to Liverpool's reluctance to sell, with the German champions instead going on to sign Ismael Saibari from PSV. In quotes published on his CfBayern Insider website, Bild's head of football Christian Falk has now shed further light on Bayern's interest in Ngumoha, claiming that the Bavarians remain in contact with the youngster's camp. “There were talks, his brother talked with FC Bayern, but it was a difficult situation for Bayern Munich. It was not clear if Liverpool would sell him or not. The price wouldn’t have been extremely high. So, you see, the club’s decision-makers feel he’d be a great option for Bayern Munich, which is why Ngumoha is still on Bayern’s shortlist," Falk said. “In the end, they had to decide for Ismael Saibari. Rio would have been complicated, so they just looked to seal the comparatively easier transfer of the two. Bayern are still in talks with Ngumoha’s camp, however, and he could be an option for the summer.” The young winger has made 14 appearances for Liverpool in all competitions this season, providing two assists.

item.title: De Gea’s Fiorentina tenure nearly over as Viola prepare to move on from ex-Man Utd goalkeeper
item.description: De Gea’s Fiorentina tenure nearly over as Viola prepare to move on from ex-Man Utd goalkeeper David De Gea’s time at Fiorentina could be coming to an end, with the Viola already looking at possible replacements for the former Manchester United goalkeeper. A ccording to Corriere dello Sport , the club have growing doubts about the 36-year-old because of his errors this season and his €3.5m net-a-year salary. Paolo Vanoli defended his captain after Sunday’s 2-2 draw with Juventus , insisting De Gea isn’t a problem. Even so, the Spaniard was at fault for Gleison Bremer’s goal in the 66th minute, when he started to come off his line for a cross and then stayed put. He has also made mistakes against Sassuolo, Como, Genoa, Frosinone and Roma, and coming for crosses, long a weakness, appears to have got worse with age. Tommaso Martinelli is the first option. The Fiorentina-owned goalkeeper is currently on loan at Serie B side Avellino. The club are also exploring the international market, and River Plate’s Santiago Beltrán, born in 2004, is among the names being linked. item.title: Vincent Kompany returns to Bayern training ground with arm in a sling after collapse
item.description: Vincent Kompany has returned to Bayern Munich ’s training ground for the first time since his collapse . The 40-year-old fell ill during a reserve-team training session on Friday 23 October and was taken to hospital, where he was diagnosed with meningeal irritation . He had been unwell with a viral infection earlier that week, which forced him to miss the pre-match press conference ahead of Bayern’s visit of Arsenal in the Champions League. He was able to be on the touchline for that match, which took place two days before his collapse, but he was nevertheless subdued in the dugout. Vincent Kompany had already been struggling with a virus leading up to his collapse (Getty) The Bundesliga champions’ director of sport Max Eberl said his return would take “weeks, not days” as Bayern insisted he would only return when he was back to full health. And on Tuesday morning, Kompany was spotted at Bayern’s Sabener Strasse training complex, with German newspaper Bild circulating photos of the Belgian in the club’s offices. He appeared to have his left arm in a sling, which is said to be due to a dislocated shoulder suffered during the fall. The club have not yet put out a statement confirming his return. The Independent has contacted Bayern Munich for comment. More photos of Vincent Kompany back at his office at Säbener Straße today [📸 @BILD ] pic.twitter.com/UCl5D9KXIj — Bayern & Germany (@iMiaSanMia) November 10, 2026 Kompany could now be in contention to make his comeback in the dugout when Bayern host Koln on Friday 20 November after the international break. The club have won four and drawn one since assistant manager Aaron Danks took the reins from Kompany, only dropping points in a dramatic 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund in Der Klassiker. Bayern are top of the Bundesliga table with 21 points in nine games, level on points with Dortmund but ahead on goal difference. During Kompany’s time away, Bayern talisman and England captain Harry Kane has also brought the Ballon d’Or back to Bavaria , pipping Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to football’s top individual prize. Harry Kane won the Ballon d’Or three days after Kompany collapsed (Getty) Kane paid tribute to Kompany in his acceptance speech , who was still in hospital at the time. He said: “To Vinnie, I know he's at home or I think still in the hospital so wishing you very well. Hope this has gave you a bit of energy. “To Vinnie and all the staff, the way we train, the way you push us, it's a credit to yourself. Since I've been with you, I've improved as a player, no doubt, improved as a person, as a leader, and that's thanks to your leadership.”

item.title: ‘Take the blame’ – Former NBA champion calls Doc Rivers ‘weird’ for Giannis Antetokounmpo comments
item.description: Photo by Tim Nwachukwu/Getty Images Doc Rivers’ seemingly critical comments about Giannis Antetokounmpo have created massive discourse, and one former Laker has taken exception to what he said. It is very rare that people within the NBA fraternity speak negatively about one another to the media. Whatever the issues are behind the scenes, they tend not to come out. So when Doc Rivers was recently critical of his former superstar, Giannis Antetokounmpo, the situation blew up quickly. Rivers made comments about the difficulty of coaching the Greek Freak and seemingly called out his playing style. Antetokounmpo was visibly shocked when told of the comments, calling them ‘insane’. Doc has since reportedly apologised, but fans and the media alike have a lot to say about the issue. Metta Sandiford-Artest asks coaches to stop blaming players after Doc Rivers’ comments The relationship between players and coaches in the NBA can be tenuous at times. It is rarely worse than when a team with expectations fails to deliver, like the Milwaukee Bucks did during Rivers’ tenure. There is plenty of blame to go around in those situations, and nobody really wants it. Regardless, for Rivers to suggest openly that Giannis is difficult to coach is something a lot of people have taken issue with. And former NBA champion Metta Sandiford-Artest has vocalised the issue. “Weird that a person would throw Giannis Antetokounmpo under the bus,” Sandiford-Artest wrote in a post on X. “Makes no sense. All he does is work hard and (bring) championships to the Milwaukee. Coach Metta so ready to take the blame. Coaches, stop blaming players.” The former Laker currently works as a coach in women’s college basketball, which may explain why he is weighing in on the matter. Rivers himself has clarified his comments since he made them, but that doesn’t mean that everyone in the basketball world will let them slide. Read more: ‘Life is short’ – Stephen A. item.description: MANCHESTER, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 08: Michael Carrick, head coach / manager of Manchester United reacts during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Manchester United and Aston Villa FC at Old Trafford on November 08, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good Tuesday morning, TSFers! I read that 20 of Arsenal’s 25 first team players are out on international duty. Noni Madueke was a weird omission from the England lineup. Bukayo Saka and William Saliba aren’t fit. So that’s the two backup keepers then. My goodness. This squad is insanely deep and talented. The news of the day (yesterday) was that Manchester United plan to sack Michael Carrick. Sure, whatever. You do you, fam. I don’t think that Carrick is the problem at that club. The move will likely improve the team because the players had quit on him and the situation had become untenable. If you’re the next manager, how could you have any confidence that the leadership core of that roster won’t quit on you if they wake up on the wrong side of the bed? My opinion: Manchester United’s players are nowhere near good enough to do what is expected of Manchester United players, i.e. compete for trophies. They haven’t been for a while. Giving Bruno Fernandes the Premier League POTY award was a joke. For the few of you who were curious, I intended to sit the Vikings defense but forgot. Better to be lucky than good, they scored a handful of points anyway. That Vikings offense is bad , which is a shame because their defense is really good. Staying in NFL-land: the Jaguars are going for it, eh? Will this be the Bills’ year? Or will someone like the Bears win the Super Bowl because the AFC beats the tar out of each other in the playoffs and softens up whoever wins that conference?

item.title: John Harbaugh, Giants Given ‘Trust’ Warning About Trade Plans
item.description: John Harbaugh and the New York Giants have been given a warning about "trade trust" before the deadline. Getty John Harbaugh sounds increasingly open to adding fresh talent before the 2026 NFL trade deadline at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, but his best-laid plans could be undone if the New York Giants don’t heed a warning about losing “trust” with potential trade partners around the league. The note of caution is sounded by “NFL Blue Book” Substack writer and All-Pro voter Charles Robinson. He pointed out how the Giants and Harbaugh “have now exposed *two* failed behind-the-curtain trade pursuits inside 1 week, between their Simmons and Taylor efforts. Whether fans like it or not (or reporters), this is the kind of thing that turns future trade partners off. Expose failed deals, lose trade trust.” #Giants have now exposed *two* failed behind-the-curtain trade pursuits inside 1 week, between their Simmons and Taylor efforts. Whether fans like it or not (or reporters), this is the kind of thing that turns future trade partners off. Expose failed deals, lose trade trust. 💯% https://t.co/G62C1azPvb — Charles Robinson (@CharlesRobinson) November 9, 2026 It’s a valid concern after it became public the Giants took a two-draft pick trade package for Indianapolis Colts’ running back Jonathan Taylor off the table. This news was on the heels of Harbaugh freely admitting to going around Tennessee Titans’ general manager Mike Borgonzi to try and swing a deal for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . The way the Giants approached a potential deal for Simmons, by going directly to owner Amy Adams Strunk, raised the concerns about trust Robinson cited. Those concerns could prove damaging on a day when Harbaugh remains blunt about adding to his playoff-chasing team. He’s still searching for reinforcements at two key spots. John Harbaugh’s Risking ‘Trust’ With Brazen Trade Strategy The reason the Giants couldn’t land Simmons ahead of the Chicago Bears “really came down to trust,” according to Robinson . He noted how “the Titans were trying to keep talks regarding Simmons as quiet as possible.” Robinson doesn’t “think the Titans trusted the Giants to keep the talks private. I think Tennessee believed that any unsuccessful talks with the Giants would have been leaked. And frankly, given what has unfolded since the trade went down, I think the Titans were right.” Keeping things private so those involved in a trade can save face, even when talks go nowhere, creates goodwill between teams. Especially when talks go nowhere. The Giants have been reckless with this goodwill twice, but Harbaugh isn’t wavering in his direct approach. Instead, the Super Bowl-winning former head coach of the Baltimore Ravens remains committed to not waiting to improve the Giants’ roster. Harbaugh told reporters on Monday, November 9, “The now weighs more important than the future, if you’re gonna put it on a scale. And you go from there,” per Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News

The development pathway is clear in the country, with young players on average making their senior club debut about three years later than those in England, for example. As a model, it is more akin to that of the NFL, and can bring benefits in preparing individuals for life after rugby – take the former wing Kenki Fukuoka, who burned brightly in a six-year international career before retiring at the age of 28 to become a doctor. These are fascinating times more generally for Japanese rugby, too. Changes to the eligibility of international players within the Japan Rugby League One are set to be introduced for the next campaign, which may limit opportunities for overseas players and – more controversially – naturalised citizens. That may in part explain the raft of Springboks announced to be returning to South Africa in recent weeks, although other factors are at play. item.title: Germany's AfD and The Left in favour of Russia at ice hockey worlds
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Fans wave German flags during the Deutschland Cup Ice Hockey match between Germany and Slovakia at the PSD Bank Dome. (is associated with: «Germany's AfD and The Left in favour of Russia at ice hockey worlds») Markus Lenhardt/dpa German far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party and The Left have spoken in favour of the participation of Russia in the 2027 men's ice hockey championships in Germany. "We consider this a return to normality. Of course, visas should also be granted to the Russian athletes," Jörn König, the AfD parliamentary group's sports policy spokesman, told the news portal ZDFheute.de. König, who has condemned the Moscow's war in Ukraine, also pointed out that the United States are never excluded from international competition, even though the nation has waged "wars in violation of international law." The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) opted to continue to exclude Russian teams from competition on security grounds. But Russia appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), which ruled in the country's favour. The backlash against the CAS decision has spread through sport, politics and business. The Left believes the CAS ruling should be accepted. "We must no longer ignore this regrettable reality," said Christian Görke, the party's spokesman on sports policy. He pointed out that Russian athletes are now competing again in other sports. A spokesperson for State Minister for Sport Ronald Rauhe told ZDFheute.de that Russia's participation would make hosting the world championships "virtually impossible for sporting and economic reasons." Germany initially threatened to give back the hosting rights for the tournament, but the country's ice hockey boss said on Sunday this is no longer an option. "We want to hold the world championship in Germany next year, and I am also very optimistic that we will manage that," German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) chief executive Frank Lutz told reporters. However, participating nations, such as world champions Finland, have threatened to boycott the tournament in case Russia is allowed to participate. Media reports say Russia is being persuaded to pull out after nations and also sponsors threatened a boycott.

item.title: Browns punter Corey Bojorquez is quietly having a Pro Bowl year
item.description: The Cleveland Browns are having a roller coaster of a season. They have beaten only one good team , the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4, defeated four other clubs considered mediocre, and lost to two bad teams . And now they are faced with some difficult games on their schedule, namely playing their division foe, the Cincinnati Bengals, twice. RELATED: BOJORQUEZ INTERVIEW Consider the fact that there aren’t any really good teams left on their schedule. Could they still make the playoffs? A division title seems out of reach, but it takes 10 or 11 wins to get that #7 seed, and they are already halfway to that goal. There are several players on the Browns roster who are having a good year. Guys like TE Harold Fannin, LBs Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams, plus DT Mason Graham are getting their fair share of press regarding possibly getting some major Pro Bowl votes. But one player stands out, and nobody is talking about his season: Browns punter Corey Bojorquez. The Boot is back 🥾 We've re-signed P Corey Bojorquez! 📰 Read more: https://t.co/wQ4NPLBAHA pic.twitter.com/r7RsK8WdCa — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) March 12, 2026 Guys who make their living on special teams are usually only noticed when they miss a field goal, or both a punt, or skip a pass to the holder. Bojo has quietly been killing it as Cleveland’s punter this season. He was re-signed during last March’s free agency period. Currently, he is listed #5 in the league in net average per punt with 44.0 yards. The league leader is just 46.1, so Bojorquez is keeping the rankings tight. He is ranked #4 in average distance per kick at 50.4. Again, the leader’s number is close at 51.8, so one game could alter these numbers. Usually, the punters with the most kicks in a season are on teams whose offensive units can’t finish drives, or are unable to sustain drives. Bojo is ranked #3 in the most punts with 43. The league leader plays for the Philadelphia Eagles, which backs up this stat goes to guys who are on struggling offensive teams. He booted a season-high eight punts in the loss to the New York Jets when the offense could not move the ball. Bojo is considered a field flipper . This means his kicks can alter the opposing team’s field position just off one punt that has traveled 50+ yards. Case in point, in Week 3 against the Carolina Panthers, Bojorquez’s first punt was for 68 yards. Pretty good, eh? His first punt of the second half was 60 yards. Then his final kick was for a whopping 81 yards that went from Cleveland’s 19-yard line into the end zone. And now they are faced with some difficult games on their schedule, namely playing their division foe, the Cincinnati Bengals, twice. RELATED: BOJORQUEZ INTERVIEW Consider the fact that there aren’t any really good teams left on their schedule. Could they still make the playoffs? A division title seems out of reach, but it takes 10 or 11 wins to get that #7 seed, and they are already halfway to that goal. There are several players on the Browns roster who are having a good year. Guys like TE Harold Fannin, LBs Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams, plus DT Mason Graham are getting their fair share of press regarding possibly getting some major Pro Bowl votes. But one player stands out, and nobody is talking about his season: Browns punter Corey Bojorquez. The Boot is back 🥾 We've re-signed P Corey Bojorquez! 📰 Read more: https://t.co/wQ4NPLBAHA pic.twitter.com/r7RsK8WdCa — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) March 12, 2026 Guys who make their living on special teams are usually only noticed when they miss a field goal, or both a punt, or skip a pass to the holder. Bojo has quietly been killing it as Cleveland’s punter this season. He was re-signed during last March’s free agency period. Currently, he is listed #5 in the league in net average per punt with 44.0 yards. The league leader is just 46.1, so Bojorquez is keeping the rankings tight. He is ranked #4 in average distance per kick at 50.4. Again, the leader’s number is close at 51.8, so one game could alter these numbers. Usually, the punters with the most kicks in a season are on teams whose offensive units can’t finish drives, or are unable to sustain drives. Bojo is ranked #3 in the most punts with 43. The league leader plays for the Philadelphia Eagles, which backs up this stat goes to guys who are on struggling offensive teams. He booted a season-high eight punts in the loss to the New York Jets when the offense could not move the ball. Bojo is considered a field flipper . This means his kicks can alter the opposing team’s field position just off one punt that has traveled 50+ yards. Case in point, in Week 3 against the Carolina Panthers, Bojorquez’s first punt was for 68 yards. Pretty good, eh? His first punt of the second half was 60 yards. Then his final kick was for a whopping 81 yards that went from Cleveland’s 19-yard line into the end zone. The NFL record for the longest punt is Steve O’Neal’s 98-yarder in 1969 while playing for the New York Jets: Take a look at Bojorquez’s 2026 season stats: Week 1 Punts: 3 Yards: 130 Yards per punt average: 43.3 Net yards per punt average: 45.0 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 48 yards Week 2 Punts: 4 Yards: 198 Yards per punt average: 49.5 Net yards per punt average: 45.0 Downed inside the 20: 2 Blocked: 0 Long: 57 yards Week 3 Punts: 5 Yards: 243 Yards per punt average: 48.6 Net yards per punt average: 45.8 Downed inside the 20: 3 Blocked: 0 Long: 62 yards Week 4 Punts: 4 Yards: 251 Yards per punt average: 62.8 Net yards per punt average: 50.3 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 81 yards Week 5 Punts: 8 Yards: 421 Yards per punt average: 52.6 Net yards per punt average: 41.8 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 67 yards Week 6 Punts: 7 Yards: 315 Yards per punt average: 48.0 Net yards per punt average: 36.7 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 62 yards Week 7 Punts: 3 Yards: 144 Yards per punt average: 48.0 Net yards per punt average: 45.0 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 59 yards Week 8 Punts: 4 Yards: 199 Yards per punt average: 49.8 Net yards per punt average: 49.8 Downed inside the 20: 3 Blocked: 0 Long: 58 yards Week 9 Punts: 5 Yards: 267 Yards per punt average: 53.4 Net yards per punt average: 39.8 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 59 yards When a running back breaks a play for 15 yards, those numbers are added to his game rushing stats. But with a punter, he could boot one for 56 yards, and then have it returned for 25 yards, which affects his net average; in this case, that stat would be 31.0 yards. Whereas a fair catch or a touchback gives the punter the exact distance of the kick. So, something the punter has zero control over can affect his overall stats. What is not considered is what kind of 56-yarder this is. Let’s say that this punt has a hangtime of 3.91 seconds and comes down in the center of the field. Even factoring in a long operation time, can one of the gunners get to the spot where the ball finally descends? Even if the gunner had nobody blocking him, there wouldn’t be a chance of this happening because that gunner would need to travel nearly 60 yards in just over 6 seconds. The punt is going to be returned. Another obstacle on a punt is if the returner doesn’t catch the ball and lets it hit the turf. We all know that because of the shape of a football, it can go almost anywhere. Including backwards. This could take off as much as 10 yards on a punt before it is downed. Yet another obstacle to getting larger numbers for punters is the pooch kick. This usually happens when the offense stalls out within 10 yards of the midfield stripe. A long field goal attempt is considered, but the coach decides it is out of the question. And the coach doesn’t want to go for it, whether that is because of field position or an unreasonable down-and-distance. So, the punter trots out. Now, there isn’t much advantage to boom the kick for a touchback, so the kicker wants the ball to land inside the 10-yard line, preferably. And if he accomplishes this, the kick itself may have been downed at the three-yard line, but the punt only traveled less than 40 yards. That is a huge plus for flipping field position for the team, but it hurts the punter’s average. The only positive stat is the “inside the 20” tabulation. But that is pretty vague in itself. There should be another stat that says “inside the 5” to distinguish punters who have the ability to make the ball travel higher so that it descends closer to the goal line. For the past eight games, Bojorquez has had at least one kick of 58 yards or longer. He routinely has contests where he has multiple punts in the 50+ range. That becomes a weapon. His talents were on full display in the loss to the New Orleans Saints . The Browns had to punt after their first possession. Bojo punted from Cleveland’s 26-yard line and was downed at the Saints’ 26. Their next possession was also a punt that went from the Browns’ 40-yard line to New Orleans’ 14-yard line. That’s flipping the field. ball back baby!!!!! #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/JJcPTOYU9p — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 8, 2026 Bojo’s only punt in Quarter 2 went to the 20-yard line, where Saints returner Barion Brown fumbled, and Cleveland safety Donovan McMillan recovered. But the kick had traveled 57 yards first. His fourth punt also went 57 yards, while his final punt in the fourth quarter traveled 59 yards from Cleveland’s 16-yard line to the Saints’ 25. This is Bojorquez’s ninth year in the league. In 202, he led the league in yards per punt average with 50.8 while with the Buffalo Bills, kicking about a third of his punts in freezing weather. In 2024, he led the league in number of punts (89) and total yardage (4,387). Last year, Bojo led the league in the same two categories, kicking 91 total punts and gaining 4,165 yards. In three different years, he had the longest recorded punt: 2020 – 72 yards, 2021 – 82 yards, and 2024 – 84 yards. He is also leading this year with that 81-yarder in the Steelers game. Three of these punts are listed in the “Top-30 NFL Punts of All Time.” And yet, with all these accolades and league-leading accomplishments, Bojorquez has never made a single Pro Bowl. This year seems promising.

item.title: Hollywood Legend LeVar Burton Has Five Special Words For WNBA Champion Gabby Williams
item.description: Nov 4, 2026; San Francisco, California, US; Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams holds the WNBA most valuable player trophy during the Golden State Valkyries championship parade. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Gabby Williams has not had a quiet week. Since the Golden State Valkyries won the WNBA championship, tributes have rolled in from sports, entertainment, and politics. Michael Jordan sent a text, Stephen Curry cheered the team on, and Barack Obama posted his praise online. Now, a Reading Rainbow legend has joined the list. LeVar Burton congratulated the Finals MVP in a short video that CBS Mornings shared on X. Both were guests on the broadcast. Burton was there to discuss his memoir, Take My Word For It, while Williams was celebrating the Valkyries’ historic run. Burton kept it brief, but the warmth came through. He shook Williams’ hand and delivered his message. “ Congratulations. Really. And I’ve got to say, you are carrying this like a queen. You really are ,” Burton said. “ Congratulations. Many more years of success, or as many as you would like to have. ” SPECIAL MOMENT: Legendary actor and “Reading Rainbow” host @levarburton congratulated Golden State @valkyries star Gabby Williams on her WNBA championship win. Williams was named the 2026 @WNBA Finals MVP after helping lead the Valkyries to their first championship in franchise history. — CBS Mornings (@CBSMornings) November 9, 2026 Burton then introduced his wife, Stephanie, who congratulated Williams as well. Williams answered with a simple thank-you. “ We’re going to come see you next season ,” Burton said. Burton has plenty to cheer. Golden State beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 on Oct. 31 at Chase Center. The Valkyries won the title in their second season, a feat described as the fastest by an expansion franchise in major American pro sports. Williams made it happen the hard way. She had 2 points at halftime, and Golden State trailed 30-24. She then scored 28 in the second half, a WNBA postseason record for a single half. She finished with 30. Williams said the break did not rattle her. Coach Natalie Nakase delivered a fiery message, but Williams saw a six-point gap and believed that if she got going, her team would be fine. She was right. Atlanta tied it in the fourth quarter, and Williams answered with a deep three with 2:18 left to make it 60-57. The Valkyries never trailed again. What The Title Means For Gabby Williams After 8 Seasons Of Waiting This was Williams’ eighth WNBA season and her first in Golden State, following three in Chicago and four in Seattle. The wait stretched beyond the league, too. France lost the 2024 Olympic gold medal game to the United States by one point, then lost to the Americans again in the FIBA Women’s World Cup final in September. Williams also won the EuroLeague title with Fenerbahçe in April. Even so, the WNBA trophy was the one she wanted most. The Finals MVP averaged 19.6 points and 2.6 steals in the series.

item.title: From W-M to the No 10, shirt numbers tell a story of football’s tactical evolution
item.description: In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, as well as the attributes a player was supposed to demonstrate Ultimate 1-50: check out our complete list of players Numbers have a fascination. The No 10 is revered almost everywhere, but perhaps most especially in Argentina, where it denotes the playmaker, the enganche , the quasi-mythical figure who links the front and back of the team. Liverpool and Manchester United have reasons to celebrate their No 7. Ajax retired No 14 for Johan Cruyff, Milan their No 3 and No 6 for Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi respectively and Birmingham their 22 for Jude Bellingham as gestures of respect for their abilities. Other numbers have been retired to mark premature deaths: the No 20 at Liverpool for Diogo Jota, the No 23 at Manchester City for Marc-Vivian Foé, the 21 at Espanyol for Daniel Jarque. But numbers are not just about individuals. In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, and the expectations of particular numbers in particular cultures, as well as the attributes a player in that shirt was supposed to demonstrate, themselves tell a story of tactical evolution. item.title: Football Daily | Manchester United, Aston Villa and the unseriousness of a 4-4 draw
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Precisely 13,266 games have been played since the inception of the Premier League, and 19 of those matches have finished 4-4 (0.1%), a rarity in a division dominated by the mighty 1-0 (17.6%). It was about time we got one, though. The months of August and September, when teams are still fighting to define their top-flight seasons and fitness and motivation tend to be at their peak, have never seen a single 4-4 draw. As motivation decreases the chances of stupid scorelines increase, and that’s where the 4-4 creeps in. There’s a certain on-the-beachness inherent in the score, and it is no coincidence that it has occurred more in the second half of April, as thoughts drift to the close season and the ineffable pointlessness of a lot of late-campaign football becomes unavoidable, than in the entirety of any other month. Students, teachers and visitors at the University of Queensland can view the world’s longest-running experiment. The flamin’ pitch drop experiment began in 1930 and is designed to demonstrate how an apparent solid (pitch) behaves like an extremely viscous liquid. Nearly 100 years ago pitch was placed in a funnel and kept at room temperature. It moves incredibly slowly at a rate of approximately one atom per second (slower than the continental drift), and only nine drips have ever been recorded , though never witnessed. Without the need for intercontinental travel, perhaps other readers can now appreciate what it’s like to watch Arsenal win 1-0 ” – John Holtom. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: That’s a Mora: Rodrigo and Roma rise with Lazio to give Eternal City new life | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Roma and Lazio have both made unbeaten starts to the Serie A season, giving those in the Italian capital dreams of a Scudetto After nine games in 28 days, Gian Piero Gasperini finally got a moment to pause and reflect on Sunday night. The Roma manager was back in Liguria, where he worked for the best part of a decade across two stints at Genoa, to collect an award from Stelle Nello Sport – an association formed to promote sport in the region – celebrating his career achievements and commitment to courageous attacking football. The timing worked out well. Gasperini’s Roma thumped Sassuolo 3-0 on Saturday, bouncing back from a midweek defeat against Manchester United . That result meant the Giallorossi had scored 31 times in 11 Serie A games. In the past 65 years only two Italian teams – the Juventus and Napoli sides of 2017-18 – had made a more prolific start to a top-flight campaign. More importantly, Roma’s victory meant they remained undefeated in domestic competition this season. Just like their neighbours Lazio, who drew 1-1 away against Napoli in the early kick-off on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.description: Midfielder’s spectacular strikes rescued a frustrating day, only for celebrations to reignite dialogue that has followed him through his career It was just what they needed at just the right time. For a tricky first half and beyond, Elversberg had been a stone in Borussia Dortmund’s shoe, the promoted side not just keeping the home team at bay but keeping them honest, nourishing ambitions of their own. “The fatigue was clearly visible,” the sporting director, Ole Book, said to Sky after a week which had contained Der Klassiker in Munich and a hard-fought Champions League victory against Betis. “We were a bit too focused on managing the game, which was understandable.” Enter Felix Nmecha. BVB have enjoyed a largely excellent start to the season, are unbeaten and level on points with Bayern Munich at the top; Bayern lead, unsurprisingly, thanks to their superior goal difference. It is a gap which has been widened by Dortmund being far from prolific, a facet which looked as if it might undercut their efforts to roll over their visitors on Saturday, especially in the absence of the injured centre-forward Serhou Guirassy. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
